spec.name: integrator
spec.intent:
Census @406cd7d0 (source identical through 8d0572f6: only records/ changed; re-derive any count or line number below if a listed path changed since). Realize `integrator position`: the role that makes each landing durable on the shared line, one per bound plan and warm across its waves. At census no role or agent holds it. packages/canon/src/skills/deliver/skill.ts:76 declares `integrator : P ⇀ agent ⟨one per P · runs gate ∧ integrate ∧ carries the state moves self decided, ¬ decides them⟩` with no role behind it (compare :79, `assayer : unit ⇀ agent ⟨role = assayer · …⟩`). The corpus projects 7 agents (architect, assayer, implementer, kino, mav, nico, planner), and none of them holds it; in practice the architect session did this work itself, which is the descent the architect position forbids.

THE POSITION (every artifact below states this, in the corpus's own register). It runs the project's whole check (deliver's `gate`: every suite, typecheck and build) ONCE per landing, on the MERGED tree. It merges a unit's commits into main only when that check is green. It runs the plan state-move verbs the architect hands it (plan advance, bind and close, verbatim, carrying the architect's --author, --reason and --cause), never choosing one itself, and it commits the records/ files they write, together with any design records the architect wrote, by pathspec. It reports the gate's result to the architect in ONE line: green, or red naming the failing check and its owner (the unit whose outputs the failing check covers). It never decides: it does not accept or reject, amend the design, or choose what is dispatched or which verb runs. It never builds, edits or repairs a unit: a red gate goes back to the architect, who routes it to the implementer that owns it. It never reads an artifact to judge it, because the assay is the assayer's. A merge is durability, not acceptance. Releasing and pushing stay the operator's sign-off, so it never tags, publishes or pushes. Plan architect-position (its architect-role and architect-skills units) states the other side of this contract: the architect decides bind, advance and close and runs no plan verb itself, its role sign routes ⟨gate · merge · commit · state-record⟩ ↦ integrator, and deliver gains the law that the integrator is never self.

CHANGE.
(1) New /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share/packages/canon/src/dimensions/role/integrator.ts, `export const integrator: Role`. It is the contract in the form its four siblings use: `integrator ≜ reads⟨…⟩ → writes⟨…⟩`, the stratum line, `reserves ⟨…⟩`, and the prohibitions. Its writes must NOT admit authoring an artifact. The purview judge's rubric (hooks/purview-guardrail.ts, 'a write whose codomain is artifact by a holder whose writes set excludes artifact') must be able to BLOCK a Write or Edit by this holder, while its reserves name the gate, merge-on-green, state-record and commit, so those acts pass. The anchor is `integrator`: it becomes `Agent.holds` through anchorOf (roles/hold.ts:116), which is the key forge routes on.
(2) New /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share/packages/canon/src/roles/integrator.ts, `export const integratorRole: RoleCell`, mirroring roles/assayer.ts and roles/implementer.ts. guardrails: [honesty]. actions: [file-ops], because this is the position whose work IS the vcs clause `main ⇒ green`. objective: `delivery ⟨end-to-end integrated green⟩`. capabilities: WITHOUT software-engineering, which is the structural statement that it does not build (the architect's own omission is the precedent); use verification-testing, operations-delivery, or both. satisficing: satisfice. autonomy: no `principal-self`, and no `handoff`, whose report shape (conclusion, evidence, action-item tail) contradicts the one-line report; the role contract states the one-line report instead. No workflow skill, following the implementer precedent: its decisions are made for it, and the architect's dispatch carries each verb. Every choice carries a comment in the file's own register, as its siblings' choices do.
(3) New /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share/packages/canon/src/agents/integrator.ts, `holds(integratorRole, { name: 'integrator', description, archetype, provenance: { mark } })`, mirroring agents/assayer.ts. The mark is an emoji and hue no other agent uses (census marks: 🏛️ blue, 🔬 red, 🔧 white, 🎬 magenta, ✈️ green, 📐 cyan, 🗺️ yellow). The description is the dispatch router's selection line: it says what the agent does and states the prohibitions out loud, following the assayer's 'NOT A REVIEWER' precedent. The nearest familiar shapes a dispatcher reaches for are a CI bot that also fixes and a release manager that pushes.
(4) /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share/packages/canon/src/skills/deliver/skill.ts, line 76 ONLY: the integrator line names its role, `⟨role = integrator · one per P · …⟩`, as line 79 does for the assayer. Every other line of that file belongs to plan architect-position (unit architect-skills). Do not touch the executor spellings, 105-122, 136-137, 148, 151-158, 162 or the header comments. Whichever plan lands second re-derives this file's census.
(5) /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share/packages/canon/src/hooks/purview-guardrail.ts: the three places that enumerate legitimate routes name the integrator. They are the comment at :34 ('WHAT IT PASSES: a dispatch to a planner, a dispatch to an assayer'), the residue at :47 (`dispatch ↦ plan ∨ assay`), and the denial feedback at :223-228 (in both the route list and the 'Legitimate and NOT blocked' list, a gate run, merge or commit goes to an integrator). Then regenerate /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share/packages/canon/targets/guardrail/purview-guardrail.sh with `pnpm canon:project:targets` (cwd /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share). Until that ruling revises it, this spec encodes the plan's recommendation: omp `task`, claude `sonnet`. /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share/packages/forge/src/adapters/omp/render.ts OMP_NEAREST_ROLE (:250-253) gains `integrator`. /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share/packages/forge/src/adapters/claude/render.ts CLAUDE_ROLE_TIERS (:74-79) gains `integrator`, and its doc comment (:63-73) says why. test/adapters/omp.test.ts (the table at :1213-1229) and test/adapters/claude.test.ts (the it.each at :695-707 and the alias list at :719-723) gain the integrator row. In /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share/docs/role.md the position catalog (:64-65) names five positions, and one new section records the integrator position: what it is, why it exists, and that it holds no workflow skill. It is a dated record and stays unchanged unless a line there claims the position has no holder.
